column1: # Required operational cutover gates. Status is `open` or `complete`; the third field records the missing proof or completed evidence.

column3: The CI rehearsal backs up a live-WAL disposable current-schema database with the production helper, verifies SQLite/metadata/hash immutability, forces an unhealthy Rust start, and restores the retained Python image; explicit Python and Rust-only redeploy paths use the same service.

CI now proves built-image startup health, a typed loopback interaction plus committed app_kv write, stopped-state failure detection, and automatic retained-Python rollback; the sole residual is a concrete Serenity/Discord HTTP write and health proof in an isolated staging guild without Python running.

Rust-owned clean/existing SQLite initialization, migration, and admission are implemented by cama-db::schema_manager and cama-runtime::gateway::SqliteDatabaseAdmission; gate remains open until every repository adapter has old/current-schema A/B delta coverage with Python stopped, including migration differential and retained-Python interoperability.
Make cama-rust serve the live gateway as sole runtime and prove command schemas, interaction timing, visibility, mentions, components, attachments, and errors with Python stopped.
Replay recorded OpenDota, Dotabase, Steam asset, and LLM provider success/failure/fallback contracts without live CI network.
Implement production renderers and pass semantic, pixel/perceptual, font, animation, and attachment-retry comparisons.
Provide health metrics, structured logs, deploy metadata, alerting, and a post-deploy verification checklist.
Register persistent views and prove buttons, modals, pagination, restart recovery, stale callbacks, and reconnect behavior.

The bounded current-schema A/B runner scripts/production_snapshot_ab_delta.py passes on two independent Python-migrated copies for guild config, Dig inventory/route, and Survey delivery; eight committed Rust snapshot twins cover the normalized row-delta, invariant, source-immutability, retained-Python-before-Rust, and retained-Python readback probes. Gate remains open for old-schema coverage, all repository families, and complete retained-Python rollback/readback transitions.

Current evidence includes the 13-family Python-seed → Rust-read/write → Python-read bridge and eight current-schema snapshot A/B replay twins; gate remains open until every transition schema and Rust write path is proven readable by the retained Python artifact after cutover, including complete rollback/readback ordering.

One fail-closed BOT_RUNTIME selector swaps only the existing bot implementation; CI and offline deploy rehearsals prove identical UID/volume/environment/GIT_SHA/SSH handoff, Rust-only redeploy without Python, and retained-image Python restoration.

All ten production background tasks are composed behind READY under the shared WorkerSpec supervisor; 79 worker tests plus runtime_lifecycle prove startup catch-up, bounded retry/restart, durable idempotent recovery, cancellation, reconnect, and graceful joined shutdown, including persisted Dig-weather broadcast recovery.
Both images acquire /app/data/.cama-runtime.lock before DB or gateway startup; bidirectional fs2/flock tests and CI/local container overlap smoke reject the second runtime and prove no DB is created.

Current production wiring uses concrete existing-schema SQLite adapters for the durable repositories audited so far; gate remains open pending a complete production-callsite inventory, replacement of any remaining durable in-memory store, and transactional SQLite/Python interoperability tests for every persistent repository family (excluding intentional process-local/session state and ephemeral planners).
